To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

CD47 is a new mediator of PMN tranepithelial migration and represents an exciting new potential therapeutic target for down regulating PMN tranepethial migration in inflammatory bowel disease and other diseases characterized by active inflammation of mucosal surfaces.

CD47 is a basolateral membrane glycoprotein that is expressed on intestinal epithelial cells and neutrophils and mediates post-adhesion events required for PMN transepethial migration across intestinal epithelial monolayers.
CD47 mediates postadhesive events required for transepithelial neutrophil migration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of transepithelial neutrophil migration.
the molecular and cellular biology of the intestinal epithelium.
the mechanisms by which neutrophils (polymorphonuclear leukocytes, PMN) migrate across polarized intestinal (T84) epithelia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CD47 represents a novel target for therapeutic intervention in mucosal inflammation, and that CD47 is a potential target in the treatment of active inflammatory disease of the mucosal surfaces.
CD47 is involved in the post adhesive events of PMN tranepithelial migration.
CD47 is a new and important molecule in the process of PMN migration across the intestinal epithelium.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

CD47 is a novel epithelial adhesion molecule that mediates postadhesion events required for neutropil migration across polarised epithelia, and that this process is inhibited by C5/D6, a novel monoclonal antibody that recognizes CD47.
CD47 is an adhesion molecule on epithelial cells and on neutrophils.
CD47 is an epithelial cell surface protein that is involved in the transmigration of neutrophils across epithelial cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
CD47, which is a ubiquitous molecule expressed on most cell types in the body, is required for neutrophils to cross epithelial barriers, and that it does so in a post-adhesive fashion.
CD47 is a new target for the treatment of inflammatory bowel disease.

we have identified a new mechanism for neutrophil transmigration across epithelial cells, namely that CD47 is involved in post-adhesive events that are required for neutrophils to cross epithelial monolayers.
